entries.title: Exodus 8:6
segments: God can make even the meanest of his creatures instruments of punishment to those who rebel against him; and none are so exalted that they can resist him and prosper.  Though for a time he waits upon them, not willing that they should perish, yet "he that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy."

entries.title: Exodus 8:9
segments: Glory over me; or, according to many, Appoint me a time.

entries.title: Exodus 8:13
segments: Villages; yards, or grounds about the houses of the Egyptians.

entries.title: Exodus 8:15
segments: He hardened his heart; by refusing to obey God.  Here the hardening of his heart is ascribed to Pharaoh, and yet the process was probably the same as when it was ascribed to God.

In one sense it was ascribed to God, and in another to Pharaoh. 
 
Those misgivings, confessions, resolutions, and promises which are extorted only by the endurance of present or the fear of future evils, are not to be depended on.  When those evils or fears are removed, their apparent good effects will be like the morning cloud or early dew, which quickly pass away.

entries.title: Exodus 8:16
segments: Lice; the word translated lice is by many supposed to mean gnats.

entries.title: Exodus 8:18
segments: The magicians did so; smote the earth to bring forth lice.  Some suppose that as they had no previous warning of this plague, and no time to prepare their deceptions, they could not imitate this miracle even in appearance; and to hide their shame, confessed that it was the effect of divine power.

entries.title: Exodus 8:21
segments: Swarms of flies; the word in the original, translated swarms of flies, means, according to some, a mixed multitude of noisome insects; according to others, a particular kind of insect.

entries.title: Exodus 8:22
segments:
Sever; separate. 
 
However great the calamities which God brings upon his enemies, he is ever able and willing to protect his people and deliver them from temptations, while he reserves the wicked to the day of judgment to be punished.  And though now they may often seem to be in many respects alike, yet hereafter all men will return and discern between him that serveth God and him that serveth him not.

entries.title: Exodus 8:24
segments: This word is most naturally understood of the destruction of the products and wealth of the land.  For this reason some suppose that it here denotes a species of beetle, common in Egypt, that devours whatever comes in its way.

entries.title: Exodus 8:26
segments:
Meet; suitable, fit, proper. 
 
  Sacrifice the abomination; various animals were worshipped by the Egyptians, and should they see the Israelites sacrifice them they would be greatly offended.
